title: Washing
hookLine: water on your face recalls your baptism
tomorrow: why pause before the first bite of breakfast?

lines: A FONT BY THE FRONT DOOR.
WHAT DOES IT HAVE TO DO WITH BAPTISM?
cards: Cold water on the face: the cheapest reset there is. Two splashes and the fog lifts a little.
Some Catholic homes keep a small font of holy water by the front door, and people touch it and make the sign of the cross on the way out. A few drops, a few seconds.
So what does a splash of water have to do with baptism, something that happened once, maybe when you were too small to remember?

teach.b: Here's the question underneath: how do you remember something that happened once? Catholics teach that baptism is given once and can't be repeated; it marks a person for good.
But it can be remembered, and water is how the tradition remembers it.
Paul calls baptism "the laver of regeneration": a washing that makes new. At some Sunday Masses the priest sprinkles the people with water, in memory of baptism.
A finger in the holy water at the church door, then the sign of the cross, is the same thing in miniature. So the line baptized again means remembered again, not done twice.
And the morning splash can carry the same thought: I was washed once, and I'm still that person. Now a neighbor who washes too. Muslims wash before prayer, a washing called wudu.
The Qur'an, in Pickthall's translation: "When ye rise up for prayer, wash your faces, and your hands up to the elbows."
And a saying of the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, in Sahih Muslim, pictures sins leaving with the drops of water.
Shared: water before standing before God, and the hope of being made clean.

One honest difference: wudu is repeated before each prayer and is part of what makes that prayer valid, while a Catholic baptism is given once, and the water afterward is a reminder, not a requirement.
Two traditions, both reaching for water as they turn toward God.

how: Catholics bless themselves with holy water on entering a church, some keep a small font at home, and at some Sunday Masses the priest sprinkles the people with water in memory of baptism.

games.q: at your cousin's baby's baptism, your little brother asks to be baptized again too, because he likes the water part. what do you tell him?
o: baptism happens once, but holy water at church helps you remember yours.
sure, Catholics get baptized again every Easter to renew it.
water only matters for babies; grown-ups don't need it anymore.
games.why: the Church teaches baptism can't be repeated, and at some Masses the people are sprinkled with water in memory of it.

practice: If there's water near you, a glass, a sink, a bottle, touch a little of it to your forehead, slowly, and notice how cool it is. Remember one thing about yourself that was true long before today.
If you're baptized and you pray, you can make the sign of the cross with wet fingers; if not, let the water simply mark a fresh start.

wordCard.voice: Washing. Water on the face as a daily reminder of the washing Catholics call baptism.

orig.note: Latin: a washing, a bath. Titus 3:5 in the Vulgate: lavacrum regenerationis.

carryVoice: Your line: baptized again. Not a second baptism, just a fresh remembering, every morning at the sink. Stay well.
